questions.explanation: Painted metres rise by 150 for every 5 intersections, so the rate is 150 divided by 5, which is 30 metres per intersection. The total painted metres, or the number of rows, is not the change per intersection.
questions.hint: Take the total change, then divide by the number of steps.

questions.learningObjective: compute a slope from two points on a line
questions.stem: The memo's line passes through (2, 7) and (6, 19). What is the slope of that line?

questions.hint: Divide the vertical change by the horizontal change.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: state why slope and rate of change are the same idea
questions.stem: The planner says a slope of 3 and a rate of 3 are the same idea. Why?

options.text: The slope of a line is the rate at which the vertical quantity changes
A rate must be a whole number before it can be a slope
options.misconception: believes rates must be whole to be slopes

options.text: Rates are measured in units while slopes are measured in no units
options.misconception: claims a slope carries no unit at all

options.text: A slope is only the rate between the first and last point shown
options.misconception: restricts a slope to the extreme points

questions.explanation: The slope of a line is the change in the vertical quantity for each unit of the horizontal one, so it is a rate of change. Slopes may be fractional, both carry units, and any two points agree.
questions.hint: A slope measures change per unit of the other quantity.
